line: The rubedo as Jung states it: the marriage of Sol and Luna, the last stage, and the reading he gives of its redness. The Self reading of the stage sits elsewhere.

sections.title: The marriage
sections.line: The red and the white are King and Queen, and the rubedo is where their marriage is consummated.

quotes.quote: The red and the white are King and Queen, who may also celebrate their “chymical wedding” at this stage
The alchemists termed this the rubedo, in which the marriage of the red man and the white woman, Sol and Luna, is consummated.
Luna in herself is spirit, and she at once joins her husband Sol, thus initiating the second and usually final stage, the rubedo.

sections.title: The way to the redness
sections.line: Two of Jung's routes to the rubedo: the heat of the fire on the whitening, and the solificatio from the blackest shade.

quotes.quote: The rubedo then follows direct from the albedo as the result of raising the heat of the fire to its highest intensity.
who has risen up from “blackest shade” to the pure whiteness of Luna and attained his redness (rubedo) through the solificatio.

sections.title: Sun and consciousness
sections.line: Jung's reading of the redness as warmth and light from the sun, and of the body taken up in the work's last image.

quotes.quote: The growing redness (rubedo) which now follows denotes an increase of warmth and light coming from the sun, consciousness.
after the manner of an Assumption and Coronation of Mary, in which the Mother of God represents the body.

sections.title: Where the Self reading sits
sections.line: The passages that tie the work's end to the unus mundus are on the unus mundus, not on the reddening itself.

quotes.quote: is none other than the “unus mundus,” the original, nondifferentiated unity of the world or of Being
But a consummation of the mysterium coniunctionis can be expected only when the unity of spirit, soul, and body is made one with the original unus mundus.
